capabilities.name: Multi-document ingestion with file-type checks, limits and hashing
capabilities.note: PDF, PNG and JPEG by their first bytes. By default 10 MB, 20 pages and 10 documents per case. Files are stored under their sha256; a rejected file becomes a limitation with a reason.

capabilities.name: Document classification
capabilities.note: Rules over words and layout. Three types have a spec at this build (bank statement, payslip, loan application), one drawn layout each; anything else is 'unknown' and says so. Wording that differs from the specs' may also read as 'unknown'. A local-model fallback is not built.

capabilities.name: Text-layer reading and OCR (offline)
capabilities.note: Every word has a box in page pixels. Scanned pages get a quality class from sharpness, not from the recogniser's score; numbers read from a degraded or poor page are flagged, not trusted. OCR output is a reading, not ground truth.

capabilities.name: Structured extraction: fields and tables, each with a confidence and a location
capabilities.note: Bank statements (digital and scanned), payslips and loan applications (digital so far), one drawn layout each. A column or label that is not found is reported as missing, never filled in. A deduction beside an empty earnings cell is not read as a row. Other document types and layouts are not built.

capabilities.name: Digital PDF forensics: comparison of saved revisions
capabilities.note: Text that differs between a PDF's earlier saved version and a later one is reported as an observation, with the old and the new text. The other digital checks are in the next row.

capabilities.name: Digital PDF forensics: covered and hidden text, pictures over text, fonts, file metadata
capabilities.note: Reported as observations with the measured values: text still in the file but drawn under a filled rectangle or a picture that comes after it (the text written over a covering rectangle is cited too); a figure or date set in a different font, size or colour from the others in its column or on its line; text that is invisible, under 2 pt or off the page; a producer or creator that names PDF-editing software; a modification date later than the creation date. Built against synthetic manipulations D2 to D5 and not yet evaluated on a held-out set. Not built: text hidden by its colour, covers that are not rectangles, bold against regular.

capabilities.name: Scan and image forensics
capabilities.note: Two checks on scanned pages that are not of poor quality, both shown as observations: words whose image grain differs from the page median, and words set out of line after the page is straightened (a word against its row, a figure's right edge against its column, a figure's height against the page's other figures). How often these checks find a changed scan is measured by the evaluation, not by the tests.

capabilities.name: Signature comparison across documents
capabilities.note: The drawn signature on each document that has a signature caption in its spec (loan application, payslip) is cut out above that caption, straightened by the page's turn if it is a scan, and compared with the signature on every other such document by shape. A pair that differs by more than the stated limit is an inconsistency with both signatures marked; every pair compared is written to the audit trail. A signature that cannot be found or read (no ink, no caption, a poor page, printed matter in the area) is a limitation, never a pass. Shapes only: it does not say who signed. Built and measured on synthetic signatures, not yet evaluated on a held-out set.

capabilities.name: Checks within one document
capabilities.note: Bank statement balance chain and dates; payslip totals, net pay against its words, and pay date against pay month; the weekday printed on a loan application. Each states its tolerance. A conflict resting on a doubtful reading is shown as a possible extraction error.

capabilities.name: Cross-document conflict checks
capabilities.note: Name, address and employer across documents, graded as passing, written differently (observation), Minor mismatch or Mismatch; account number, which matches or is a Mismatch; net pay against the credits on a statement; declared income against gross earnings; the application date against the dates of the other documents; a file submitted twice; the same producing software on different kinds of document made minutes apart. A comparison that cannot be made is reported as a limitation, never as a pass. Built for three document types with one drawn layout each, and not yet evaluated on a held-out set. Each finding prints its tolerance.

capabilities.name: Context rules (income, obligations, date windows)
capabilities.note: Two rules: monthly obligations (existing instalments plus the new loan over its tenure) as a share of declared income, and a document dated more than 90 days before the application. Both are observations for the reviewer, never conflicts. Their reference limits are synthetic values chosen for this prototype, not a lending standard, and the instalment sum ignores interest. Rules taken from a lender's own policy are not built.

capabilities.name: Relationships between findings (clusters)
capabilities.note: Findings are grouped when they cite the same extracted field, lie on the same place of a page (half of the smaller box inside the other), or concern the same name, address, employer or account number in different documents. A group is ranked by how many independent kinds of check fired in it (visual, arithmetic, cross-document, metadata): a count, not a probability. A group with two or more kinds gets a headline finding, classed as potential manipulation, that lists its members and cites each of their places once. Context rules are linked but count as no kind, and limitations are never grouped. Findings that share none of these stay apart even where a person would relate them. Not evaluated on a held-out set; the overlap limit is a starting value.

capabilities.name: Plain-language explanations and next steps from fixed templates
capabilities.note: Fixed wording per detector and class. Nothing is written by a model.

capabilities.name: Explanation wording from a local language model
capabilities.note: The guard, the client that talks only to this computer, the fallback to template wording and the audit event are built and tested with a stand-in model and a stub server. No real model has run yet, so how a small model words a group of findings is not measured. It is off unless a model is given, it words only the headline of a group of findings, it sees structured findings and no page text, and it cannot add, change or remove a finding. What it writes is used only if it cites ids it was given and states no figure, date or verdict that the evidence does not hold. It is labelled as inference.

capabilities.name: Evidence traceability: finding to file, sha256, page and box, with a marked crop
capabilities.note: Every piece of evidence names its document, page and box; the trace command prints them and checks the stored file's hash.

capabilities.name: Investigation dossier: HTML (self-contained) and JSON, with its own hash
capabilities.note: Observations, inconsistencies, potential-manipulation candidates and limitations are kept in separate places.

capabilities.name: Dossier export as PDF
capabilities.note: Print the HTML dossier to PDF from a browser meanwhile.

capabilities.name: Tamper-evident audit trail with a verify command
capabilities.note: Each event carries the hash of the one before it. The dossier records the trail's length and last hash.

capabilities.name: Safe failure: rejected files, failed or stuck steps become visible limitations
capabilities.note: A step that fails or times out is listed as a limitation and the case goes on. A step stuck in native code is abandoned, not killed.

capabilities.name: Offline operation
capabilities.note: The OCR models ship inside the package. The test suite runs with connections to public addresses blocked.

capabilities.name: Review interface in the browser
capabilities.note: Runs on this computer only. Upload, a background run with progress, page images with word, field and finding boxes, evidence crops, reviewer actions written to the audit trail, the audit trail, this list and the dossier download. The server side is tested; how the page behaves in a browser was checked by hand, not by an automated browser test. Findings that share evidence are grouped in the Clusters tab, each group under its headline.

capabilities.name: Handwriting and multilingual OCR
capabilities.note: Not built; text is read as printed English.

capabilities.name: Real-world document layouts at scale
capabilities.note: Only synthetic documents were used. Nothing is claimed about real ones.

capabilities.name: Logo and stamp comparison across documents of one issuer
capabilities.note: The logo (right of the issuer's name) and the stamp (above its caption) on each document whose type spec lists them (bank statement, loan application) are cut out, straightened by the page's turn if it is a scan, and compared by shape with those on every other document whose issuer line reads alike; a stamp is compared at its best turn within 8 degrees. A pair that differs by more than the stated limit is an inconsistency with both marks marked; every pair compared is written to the audit trail. A mark that cannot be found or read (no ink, no caption, a poor page, printed matter in the window) is a limitation, never a pass. Built and measured on synthetic marks only: six invented designs, two of which (the same motif in a circle and in an octagon) are not told apart, and a small change to a logo is not found. Not yet evaluated on a held-out set.

capabilities.name: Verdicts on authenticity or intent; telling who signed; photographs and identity documents
capabilities.note: Unsupported by design. The tool lists anomalies for a human reviewer and never concludes. Signatures, logos and stamps are compared by shape between documents, which does not say who signed or who issued them. Photographs and identity documents are not examined.

limitations: Every document used to build and test this tool is synthetic. Nothing was evaluated on real documents, real scanners or real layouts.
Findings are for a human reviewer. An ordinary cause (a re-issue, a rounding rule, a misread digit, an unusual layout) can produce any of them, and the tool cannot tell which.
OCR output is a reading, not ground truth. On scans a number from a degraded or poor page is not trusted, and a conflict that rests on one is shown as a possible extraction error.

The statement checks assume the oldest row comes first and that a balance follows each row. A statement listed newest first, or with signed amounts, is reported as a layout the checks do not assume and is not checked.
A totals row at the foot of a statement is not read, so it is not checked.
A transaction row that extraction misses (for example one with a garbled date on a scan) shows up as a balance break at the next row.

The saved-revision comparison reads incremental saves only. By default a linearized PDF is not compared, at most 16 revisions of a file are opened and a page of more than 5000 words is not compared; each of these is reported as a limitation.
A PDF that was saved more than once for an ordinary reason (a correction, a re-issue, a form being filled in) shows revision observations too.

The cover check looks at opaque rectangular fills, and at pictures smaller than half a page, drawn after the text they lie over. A cover of another form (a curve, a clipped path), text hidden by its colour, and the draw order of a picture on a file whose page content is unusual are not handled; a page that draws more than 5000 objects is not examined and the dossier says so. Invisible text on a page that is mostly one picture is taken as the text layer of a scan and is not reported.

The font check compares figures and dates that stand in a text run of their own with the others in their column (four or more) or on their line (three or more). A figure inside a longer run of text is not compared, and bold against regular of one family is not. A logo, stamp or signature placed as a picture on a text page is reported like any other picture.

The metadata check reads what the file says about itself: producer and creator names, creation and modification dates. Anyone who can write the file can write them, and a file saved again for an ordinary reason shows a later modification date.

The grain check compares each scanned word with the median of its page, on the paper inside the word's box and away from the ink, and leaves out paper brighter than 250 (the scanner cuts it at white). Scanners and JPEG saves change grain for ordinary reasons. On a mildly degraded scan a changed word can keep a grain close to the page's, because the second JPEG save puts back grain of about the same size, so the check finds a patch more easily on coarser scans. Pages of poor quality are not analysed and the dossier says so.

The placement check straightens a scanned page by the turn that makes its text rows sharpest, then compares each word's position with its row, and a figure's right edge and height with the page's other figures and its column. The height of a text word is not compared (its box depends on its letters and on the slant of its line). A difference counts when it is more than 6 px (position in the row) or 10 px (figure height, right edge): four times a spread that is never taken below 1.5, 2.5 and 2.5 px. Those floors come from the largest differences on 42 genuine simulated statements (3.3, 7.0 and 6.1 px on pages not degraded), and the largest right-edge difference rose from 5.6 to 6.1 px between the first six and the next eight, so a genuine statement can still give an observation, and a shift under the limits, or a row pasted from a scan turned the same way, is not seen. On a degraded page the floors are raised by half and figure columns are rarely found (one to five figures read), so the right-edge comparison is in practice not made there. A creased or curled page moves words and can give an observation. A page of poor quality, one with fewer than 12 words or no row of four words, or one turned by more than 2.9 degrees is not compared and the dossier says so. The turn is looked for up to 10 degrees either way; a page turned further than that is not recognised as turned and may be compared as if it were turned less.

A revision boundary is recognised from a startxref pointer followed by %%EOF. A file crafted to carry a convincing pointer inside a content stream can mislead it, which gives a false observation or a visible limitation, not a silent pass.

A document the tool does not recognise as one of the three supported types is left out of the comparisons across documents, and the dossier says which comparisons were not made. Wording unlike the specs' can read as unrecognised.

Names, addresses and employers are graded, not only passed or flagged: the same value apart from case, spacing and punctuation passes; the same words in another order, with other titles or with initials (names), the same comma-separated parts of an address in another order, or an employer with another legal form, are an observation 'written differently'; text at or above the similarity limit (0.85 for names, 0.8 for addresses and employers) that is still not identical is a 'Minor mismatch'; anything further apart is a 'Mismatch'. A name with a word left out (a middle name) is a Minor mismatch. The limits are starting values and have not been tuned or evaluated.

An initial stands for any name it starts, so 'M. Varghese' and 'Mohan Varghese' are reported only as written differently. An address with the same words in another order but without commas is a Minor mismatch or a Mismatch by how far apart the text is, never a difference in form; any change in the numbers of an address, or in their order, is a Mismatch. An employer with a word more or fewer apart from Pvt, Ltd and the like is a Minor mismatch at a text similarity of 0.8 or more and a Mismatch below it.

Amounts are not graded: a net pay that differs from the credit by no more than the larger of INR 1 and 0.5% of the larger amount, a declared income within 5% of the gross earnings, and a sum within a document that is off by INR 1 or less pass without a finding.

On a scan a Minor mismatch of a name or an address can be one letter misread by the OCR. On a page of good quality it is shown as a conflict with a note saying so; on a degraded or poor page it is shown as a possible extraction error to verify. Account numbers have no minor grade: they match, or they are a Mismatch.
That the employer pays the salary is judged by one word of the employer's name against the descriptions of salary credits on the statement. It is a heuristic and can be wrong in either direction.
An account number that is masked, or short, matches another by its visible end, which must be at least three characters.
A payslip dated outside every statement period submitted is reported as not compared, not as a conflict. A set of several months' statements looks the same.
The same software producing different kinds of document within ten minutes is noted, and it also happens for ordinary reasons (one office system issuing both).

The context rules use reference limits that are synthetic and illustrative (obligations up to half of declared income, documents up to 90 days old); they are not a lending standard, and the instalment sum ignores interest.
Thresholds are starting values and have not been tuned or evaluated yet.
Untrusted files are opened in the same process as the tool. Size, page and time limits apply, but there is no sandbox.
Handwriting is not analysed, and text other than printed English is not read.

The signature comparison was fitted on synthetic signatures only, drawn by the generator for 14 invented people, and its limit was set from them. It looks in a fixed area above the caption printed under the signature, sized by the caption's text, so a layout that signs elsewhere is reported as not compared or compares the wrong marks; a stamp or a ruled line in that area counts as part of the signature unless it fills the area or reaches its edge, which is reported as not compared. A speck of ink under 12 px² is dropped, and so is a small separate piece (under a tenth of the largest) that sticks out of the box of the larger pieces; a stray larger than that, or one inside the box of the signature, counts as part of it, and in a scan of 120 dpi the drop can take off the end of a thin real stroke. A scan turned by more than 2.9 degrees is not compared. It reads shape, not authorship: one person's signatures vary from signing to signing, a scan or another kind of pen changes the strokes, and a signature copied onto another document passes. A mismatch is a lead for a reviewer and nothing more.

Findings are linked only through a shared field, an overlapping place on a page, or the same name, address, employer or account value. Two unrelated findings that share a place are grouped, and a large shape drawn over several fields can join the findings on all of them, so a group can be wider than the story behind it. Findings that a person would relate by meaning but that share none of these are not linked. A group of two kinds of check can have an ordinary cause, and its review priority is a count of kinds of check, not a likelihood. The overlap limit (half of the smaller box) is a starting value that has not been tuned or evaluated.

A language model, if one is given, only words the headline of a group of findings; it does not detect, reason over the pages or change a finding. The guard reads digits: a number written in words is not checked, and a sentence can be accurate in each figure and still be a poor summary. The prompt carries finding titles and field values, which come from the documents, so a document can put its own text in front of the model; the guard, the fixed JSON shape and the label are what limit it. No real model has been run through it yet, so its wording, speed and rate of rejection are unmeasured.

The logo and stamp comparison was fitted on synthetic marks only: six invented designs of each, drawn by the generator, with both limits set from them. Two of the six logos, which share a motif and differ only in the outline, are not told apart at any limit; a small change to a logo (one point moved a tenth of its width) is not found; and the margin at the logo limit is thin (the largest genuine pair is 8.5 against a limit of 10.5). It looks in a fixed window right of the line that names the issuer (the tallest line of page 1 that reads as a name) and above the caption printed under the stamp, sized by the text beside it, so a layout that puts a mark elsewhere is reported as not compared or compares the wrong ink; a window that is mostly ink or has ink at its edge is reported as not compared. The same two drops of ink apply as for signatures. Under a short issuer name the line beneath it runs on into the logo window: its words are erased from the window, and where that line stops inside the logo (or text is printed over the logo itself) the logo is reported as not compared, because the two documents would cut it differently. Documents count as one issuer when that line reads alike (80 % likeness), so a misread or changed name leaves a document ungrouped and unchecked, and a title taller than the issuer's name, printed alike on the documents of two issuers, takes the place of the name and groups them, so their different marks are reported as a difference. When two documents carry a mark but no two share an issuer line, that is one limitation; a single marked document says nothing. A scan turned by more than 2.9 degrees is not compared, and the round stamp of a payslip is not compared. It reads shape, not origin: a mark copied from another document passes.
assumptions: Dates are read day first (DD/MM/YYYY); a date that could be read another way is marked ambiguous and given a low confidence.
Amounts are in rupees, with lakh or western digit grouping.
A usable PDF text layer is taken as read; a page whose text layer is unusable is read by OCR instead.
Boxes are pixels of the page rendered at 200 dpi unless a page says otherwise; points are pixels x 72 / dpi.
Documents are synthetic or authorised for the purpose, and one case is analysed at a time on one machine.
